rules.sentence: SFTs can occur in patients over a wide age range with peak incidence in 5th and 6th decades of life.
These tumors are rare in children and adolescents.
SFTs have been reported at almost every anatomic site.
Pleura is the most common site and accounting for approximately 30% cases.
Other frequently involved sites include meninges (27%), abdominal cavity (20%), trunk (10%), extremities (8%) and head & neck (5%).
Pleural SFTs present at somewhat older age (mean = 60.2 years) compared to meningeal (mean = 50.6 years) and extra-pleural SFTs (mean = 50.3 years).
No known risk factors for development of SFTs are currently known.
SFTs are usually asymptomatic, slow growing tumors which are often discovered as an incidental finding on imaging.
These tumors sometimes produce symptoms related to pressure effects on adjacent tissues/organs.
The diagnostic criteria for HPC were refined and features for assessment of malignancy were established by Enzinger and Smith in a large study of 106 cases.
The molecular hallmark of these tumors is the recurrent fusion of NAB2 and STAT6 genes located at chromosomal region 12q13.
Current WHO Classification of Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors has classified SFT as a fibroblastic neoplasm with intermediate (rarely metastasizing) behavior.
